description: The report cites the correct, gold-relevant transaction (perfect traceability) but draws a wrong conclusion from it.
report_text: T1-001 confirms this was a routine internal payroll transfer, not part of any fraud.
flag: This is a genuine scope limitation, not an implementation bug: evidence-traceability (precision/recall/F1) measures whether a citation points at a real, gold-relevant record -- it says nothing about whether the CONCLUSION drawn from that record is correct. Here the report is perfectly traceable (1.0/1.0/1.0) while asserting a conclusion the underlying case data does not support (T1-001 is in fact a fraud-chain transfer, not payroll). Catching a correctly-cited-but-wrongly-interpreted claim requires the qualitative judge dimensions (e.g. network_identification, typology in task-007's rubric.json), not the deterministic traceability metrics. Evidence traceability is a necessary but not sufficient signal for report correctness -- this should be stated explicitly in any methodology writeup that cites traceability scores as evidence of report quality.
